scope: candidate mathematical/source fidelity only; not fixed-task admission or a model score

assumptions: Let \(P,Q\) be two probability laws on \(\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}\) with the product sigma algebra. Let \(H_t=(X_1,\dots,X_t)\) and \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H_t)\). The finite marginals come from normalized conditional tables \(p_t(x\mid h)\), \(q_t(x\mid h)\) for \(X_{t+1}\) at each history \(h\) of length \(t\). At every \(P\)-positive history, \(q_t(x\mid h)=0\) if \(p_t(x\mid h)=0\).

The two laws use the same stopping rule \(\tau\), a stopping time of the canonical histories, with a common deterministic dummy bit after stopping. Assume \(P(\tau<\infty)=1\); do not assume \(Q(\tau<\infty)=1\). Let \(W\ge0\) be measurable on the full path space, possibly \(+\infty\) on exceptional paths, with \(\mathbb E_P W^2<\infty\). Think of \(W\) as total work, including any output-dependent terminal charge.

At a \(P\)-positive history define \[\eta_t(h)=\sum_{x:p_t(x\mid h)>0}\frac{(q_t(x\mid h)-p_t(x\mid h))^2}{p_t(x\mid h)}.\] On other histories set it to zero. For the positive result assume a deterministic \(B\ge0\) with \(\sum_{t<n}\eta_t(H_t)\le B\) simultaneously for all \(n\), \(P\)-almost surely.

This is a proposed alternative cost-transfer interface, not a statement of either paper. For source comparison the linked local TV result controls output event discrepancies under an integrable local budget and a common Markov suffix. The linked query result gives first-moment work information for one actual SPHMC phase under its own input assumptions. Neither supplies a full-path likelihood-ratio or stopped-work \(L^2\) bound.
original_source.question: Prove that the finite-prefix likelihood ratios yield a full-path density \(L=dQ/dP\) with \(\mathbb E_P L^2\le e^B\). Justify why the same stopping rule terminates \(Q\)-almost surely and show \[|\mathbb E_Q W-\mathbb E_P W|\le \sqrt{(e^B-1)\operatorname{Var}_P(W)}.\] Then audit the proposed replacement \(\sup_n\sum_{t<n}\mathbb E_P\eta_t(H_t)\le 2\): construct a two-active-call family with this averaged budget and \(\mathbb E_P W^2\le 1\), but unbounded \(\mathbb E_Q W\) across the family. Identify the additional interfaces needed before applying the positive result to the cited TV and query-work routes.
steps: Every \(Q\)-positive finite prefix is \(P\)-positive by induction from the empty prefix and the local support condition. Set \(L_0=1\) and \(L_t=Q(H_t)/P(H_t)\) on \(P\)-positive atoms, zero elsewhere. Under \(P\), \(L_{t+1}=L_t q_t(X_{t+1}\mid H_t)/p_t(X_{t+1}\mid H_t)\); the denominator is positive on the realized transition almost surely. On each positive history atom the conditional first moment of the step ratio is \(1\), and its conditional second moment is \(1+\eta_t(H_t)\), by expanding the square and using both probability sums. Thus \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb E_P[L_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]&=L_t,\\ \mathbb E_P[L_{t+1}^2\mid\mathcal F_t]&=L_t^2(1+\eta_t(H_t)).\end{aligned}\] All quantities at a fixed time are integrable on the finite positive atoms.

Set \(A_0=1\) and \(A_n=\prod_{t<n}(1+\eta_t(H_t))\). Crucially \(A_{t+1}\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and at least \(1\). Dividing the conditional square identity by this predictable quantity shows that \(L_n^2/A_n\) is a nonnegative \(P\)-martingale of mean \(1\). Since \(\log(1+x)\le x\) for \(x\ge0\), the assumed pathwise budget yields \(A_n\le e^B\) almost surely. Therefore \(\mathbb E_P L_n^2\le e^B\) for each \(n\). Replacing the random factors by their ideal-history averages would discard their dependence on the likelihood weight.

For \(m\ge n\), the first martingale identity and conditioning on \(\mathcal F_n\) give \(\mathbb E_P[L_mL_n]=\mathbb E_P L_n^2\). Hence \(\mathbb E_P (L_m-L_n)^2=\mathbb E_P L_m^2-\mathbb E_P L_n^2\). These squared norms are increasing and bounded, so the sequence is Cauchy in \(L^2(P)\). Completeness yields \(L\), nonnegative almost surely because the negative part is bounded in \(L^2\) by the distance to each nonnegative \(L_n\). Convergence also holds in \(L^1(P)\), so \(\mathbb E_P L=1\) and \(\mathbb E_P L^2\le e^B\). For a cylinder event in \(\mathcal F_n\), \(\int_E L_m\,dP=Q(E)\) for every \(m\ge n\). Passing to the limit and using uniqueness of probability measures on the generating cylinder algebra proves \(Q=L P\) on the full sigma algebra, not merely on each finite prefix.

The event \(\{\tau=\infty\}\) is measurable as the countable intersection of the events \(\{\tau>n\}\). It has \(P\)-probability zero and hence \(Q\)-probability zero. Change of measure gives \(\mathbb E_Q W=\mathbb E_P[LW]<\infty\) by Cauchy–Schwarz, with any \(P\)-null exceptional values irrelevant under both laws. Since \(\mathbb E_P(L-1)=0\), center \(W\) by its \(P\)-mean. Then \[\begin{aligned}\left|\mathbb E_Q W-\mathbb E_P W\right|&=\left|\mathbb E_P[(L-1)(W-\mathbb E_P W)]\right|\\ &\le\sqrt{(e^B-1)\operatorname{Var}_P(W)},\end{aligned}\] because \(\mathbb E_P(L-1)^2=\mathbb E_P L^2-1\). No bounded-work assumption or separate \(Q\)-termination premise has been used.

For integers \(m\ge2\) take \(p=m^{-2}\), \(q=m^{-1}\) as the first-bit probabilities of \(1\) under \(P,Q\). If the first bit is \(1\), let the second-bit law be \({\rm Ber}(p)\) under \(P\) and identically \(1\) under \(Q\); if the first bit is \(0\), use identically \(0\) for both. Stop after two bits and pad identically. Local support holds. The first budget is \((q-p)^2/[p(1-p)]=(m-1)/(m+1)\), and the second is \(m^2-1\) on the first-bit-one branch, zero otherwise. Hence the sum of ideal-history averages is \((m-1)/(m+1)+1-m^{-2}<2\); the rare branch has no uniform pathwise budget.

For \(E=\{X_1=X_2=1\}\), \(P(E)=m^{-4}\), \(Q(E)=m^{-1}\). Charge an additional terminal work \(W=m^2\mathbf 1_E\), distinct from the number of the two active calls. Then \[\mathbb E_P W=m^{-2},\qquad \mathbb E_P W^2=1,\qquad \mathbb E_Q W=m.\] The averaged budgets and ideal work second moments stay bounded but implemented expected work does not. In fact \(\mathbb E_P L_2^2\ge Q(E)^2/P(E)=m^2\); the squared likelihood has concentrated on the same rare branch that carries the large conditional error.

To transfer this argument to an actual algorithm one must identify the common stopped history space, conditional densities and absolute continuity, a genuine pathwise conditional second-moment budget, and an ideal second moment of the actual total work. The local TV comparison supplies none of these likelihood controls, and single-phase expected query work does not certify that stopped-work second moment. The alternative interface is proved here only for the stated binary path model, not established for either paper's sampler.

rubric.criterion: Constructs valid finite-prefix densities, checks local support and the two conditional moments, and obtains the correct uniform square bound with a predictable compensator (or an equivalent valid argument).
Identifies the full-path density by a justified convergence and cylinder-extension argument; transfers almost-sure termination and the centered variance estimate without assuming Q integrability.
Gives a valid family with bounded summed ideal-average budgets and unit-bounded ideal work second moment, but divergent implemented mean; verifies the actual conditional tables and work moments.

Distinguishes the added absolute continuity, pathwise likelihood and actual stopped-work second-moment interfaces from the source TV and single-phase expected-work results. Does not claim a transfer to either actual algorithm.

original_source.boundary: Original unpaired natural-language audit with a complete binary-path calculation. Not a general-state Lean theorem, not the Gaussian Cloud or SPHMC source argument, not a claim that their actual algorithms satisfy the new likelihood or stopped-work assumptions. The same public development family is retained; no held-out or calibrated-level claim.
original_source.source_note: Original Samplinglib mathematical QA over two owned supporting publications: gaussian-cloud-kernel-hybrid-telescope.json (common-suffix eventwise TV) and sphmc-implemented-phase-query-work.json (single actual phase query moments/work). It probes the explicitly excluded TV-to-unbounded-cost inference by adding a different conditional likelihood hypothesis and testing a weaker substitute. The positive result and counterexample are new exposition, not quotations or attributed paper statements. Only original project Apache-2.0 material is used, and this stays in the public adaptive-hybrid-cost-boundary family.

A.objects: Probability measures P and Q; real transition tables p and q; a real budget B; a stopping time τ; a nonnegative extended-real observable W; and an existential real-valued function L.
A.domains: The path space S is ℕ → Bool with the product measurable structure and discrete Bool. H n = Fin n → Bool. The tables p and q have type (n : ℕ) → H n → Bool → ℝ. F n is the σ-algebra pulled back by the length-n prefix map, reading coordinates 0 through n−1. The maps have types τ : S → WithTop ℕ, W : S → ENNReal, and L : S → ℝ.
A.quantifiers: The conclusion holds for every choice of P, Q, p, q, B, τ, W and the stated hypotheses. Both table normalizations apply to every n and h, including histories of zero mass. The budget is for every n, P-almost every x. One L satisfies the entire conjunction; the likelihood convergence and L's nonnegativity are P-almost everywhere, and the conclusion about τ being finite is Q-almost everywhere.
A.assumptions: P and Q are probability measures. R₁ P p and R₁ Q q give the recursion a(M,n+1,snoc(h,b)) = a(M,n,h)·t n h b for all n,h,b for the respective measure/table pairs, where a is the real prefix-event mass. R₂ P p q requires p n h b = 0 to imply q n h b = 0 whenever a(P,n,h)>0. Each table is nonnegative on Bool and sums to 1 at every history. For each n, ∑_{k<n} E P p q k x ≤ B for P-almost every x. τ is an F-stopping time and τ≠⊤ P-almost everywhere. W is measurable and its nonnegative extended integral of W² under P is finite.
A.conclusion: There exists a strongly measurable L with 0 ≤ L P-almost everywhere and MemLp L 2 P. For P-almost every x, D P Q n x converges to L x as n tends to infinity. The real integrals satisfy ∫L² dP ≤ exp B and ∫L dP = 1. As measures, Q = P.withDensity (x ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (L x)), and Q is absolutely continuous with respect to P. The set {x | τ x ≠ ⊤} is measurable and has full Q-measure. Both nonnegative extended integrals of W, under P and under Q separately, are finite. The absolute difference of their real conversions is at most √((exp B−1)·variance_P(x ↦ (W x).toReal)).
A.senses: D is Q-prefix mass divided by P-prefix mass, with real division by zero equal to zero. E is zero at histories of zero P-prefix mass; elsewhere it is the Bool sum of (q−p)²/p at the observed history, using that same division convention. The budget controls cumulative discrepancy P-almost surely at each finite horizon, not on every path and not merely in expectation. The likelihood is indexed by the deterministic prefix length n, not by τ. The assumptions do not require W to depend on τ or be measurable at τ. Absolute continuity is Q≪P only, and the Q-integrability assertion is first-moment finiteness of W, not a Q-second-moment assertion. The explicit finiteness conclusions make the conversions of both W integrals meaningful as finite reals rather than using the convention ⊤.toReal = 0.
A.constants: Prefix depth zero is empty; finite sums use k=0,…,n−1. Normalization and mean density are 1, the Lp exponent and square powers are 2, and the two bounds use exp B and exp B−1 respectively. The excluded stopping-time value is ⊤. B is real and there is no separate nonnegativity assumption on B.

B.objects: A real parameter m; scalars p=(m²)⁻¹ and q=m⁻¹; the specified tables pt=U p p and qt=U q 1; the specified observable C m; the constant stopping time x↦2; and existential measures P and Q.
B.domains: P and Q are measures on S = ℕ → Bool with the product measurable structure. Table arguments are n : ℕ, h : H n = Fin n → Bool, b : Bool, with real values and the same prefix filtration F. C m : S → ENNReal. The constant stopping time takes the value 2 in WithTop ℕ.
B.quantifiers: For every real m with 2≤m, there exist P and Q jointly satisfying the full conjunction. Each table is normalized at every n and h, with nonnegativity for every b. Separately for each of P and Q, almost every path has x k = false for every k≥2. The strict bound on the sum of discrepancy integrals holds for every n.
B.assumptions: The only external hypothesis is 2≤m. The scalars and tables are let-bound from m: U u v assigns true-probability u at depth zero, v at depth one if the first bit is true and zero there otherwise, and zero at all depths at least two; false-probability is the complement. Probability, recursion, compatibility, normalization, and stopping properties are required of the witnesses in the conclusion, not assumed as inputs.
B.conclusion: There are probability measures P and Q with R₁ P pt, R₁ Q qt and R₂ P pt qt. Both pt and qt are nonnegative on Bool and sum to 1 at all histories. The constant map x↦2 is an F-stopping time. Under P and under Q separately, all coordinates k≥2 are false almost surely. For every n, ∑_{k<n} ∫ E P pt qt k x dP(x) < 2, using ordinary real integrals. The map C m is measurable, ∫⁻ (C m)² dP = 1, and ∫⁻ C m dQ = ENNReal.ofReal m.
B.senses: R₁ is the prefix mass recursion and R₂ is the one-sided support condition only at positive-P-mass histories. E uses the same zero-mass and real division conventions as in A. The strict bound is on sums of P-integrals of E, not a P-almost-sure bound on sums along paths. C m pays ENNReal.ofReal(m²) if coordinates 0 and 1 are both true and zero otherwise; it is a terminal charge, not an observation count. The constant stopping time and the almost-sure restrictions on later coordinates are separate facts. The stated moment equalities concern the P second moment and the Q first moment; there is no asserted likelihood limit, density, or variance bound.
B.constants: The scalar threshold is m≥2; the table parameters are ((m²)⁻¹,(m²)⁻¹) for pt and (m⁻¹,1) for qt. The stopping value and tail cutoff are both 2, and the discrepancy cap is strictly less than 2 at every horizon. The P second moment is exactly 1, the Q first moment is exactly ENNReal.ofReal m, and the charge on the two-true prefix is ENNReal.ofReal(m²).
